sections.html:
Saunders County covers about 760 square miles of eastern Nebraska, and Wahoo is both the county seat and the largest city. The county counts as part of the Omaha-Council Bluffs metropolitan area, yet most of its land is farm ground, in low rolling hills that slope toward the Platte River valley on the north and east.

The 2020 census counted 22,278 residents. Wahoo had 4,818, Ashland 3,086 and Yutan 1,347. Villages include Ceresco, Mead, Cedar Bluffs, Valparaiso, Memphis, Prague and Weston, and 9,045 people, about 41 percent of the county, live outside any town. There were 9,987 housing units in 2020, with 79.6% owner-occupied.

That 41 percent matters when you sell. Plenty of Saunders County homes sit on acreage outside a city limit, where wells, zoning and road questions differ from a lot in Wahoo.

Three offices share the courthouse at 433 N Chestnut, Wahoo, NE 68066, and each does a different job. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

  • Assessor (Suite 200, 402-443-5600) values every parcel in the county.
  • Treasurer (Suite 201, 402-443-8128, mail to PO Box 337) bills and collects real estate and personal property tax and passes the money to schools, cities and other districts. A new title has to be in the door by 4:00 p.m. The same office handles motor vehicle registration and driver licensing.
  • Register of Deeds (Suite 203, 402-443-8111) records deeds and mortgages. Deeds from 1997 forward can be searched on Nebraska Deeds Online.

You can also pay through the state's Nebraska Taxes Online page for Saunders County.

sections.h2: How the assessor values a property
sections.html:
Value is set as of 12:01 a.m. on January 1 each tax year. Homes, commercial property and industrial property are valued at 100 percent of market value, and agricultural and horticultural land at 75 percent. State section 77-201 sets the 75 percent rule for farmland, with a lower 50 percent figure for school bond levies approved by voters on or after January 1, 2022.

The assessor only sets the value. The rate comes from the county board and every other taxing body, and it is applied to that value. If you disagree with a value, you work through the protest window handled by the county board, not through the Treasurer.

In the 2024 data, the county's own levy was $0.2160 per $100 of taxable valuation. It raised about $12.0 million of the roughly $75.6 million that all local governments levied, so the county board's slice is about 16 percent of what property owners pay in total.

Schools, the city or village, the natural resource district and other bodies add their own levies, so the county line is never the whole bill. The Department of Revenue posts every rate in its annual taxing subdivisions report.

sections.h2: Why similar houses pay different tax
sections.html:
The county is cut into many school districts and village limits, and each combination carries its own total levy. Thirteen school districts serve parts of the county, among them Ashland-Greenwood, Wahoo, Yutan, Mead, Cedar Bluffs, Raymond Central and North Bend Central, plus districts named for Fremont, Gretna, Schuyler, Waverly and David City. Lower Platte North and Lower Platte South are the two natural resource districts that reach in.

A buyer comparing a Wahoo address with an Ashland address, or a town lot with an acreage, should ask for the actual prior-year bill, not a county average. Electric providers also vary by location: Butler PPD, the City of Wahoo, Omaha PPD and the Village of Prague. That is a useful line in a listing or a cash-offer conversation about monthly carrying costs.

The seller pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax, and the title company settles the current year's property tax between the two sides. Under section 76-901 the tax falls on the grantor at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for transfers before January 1, 2032, then drops to $2.32. Value means the full consideration, including any liens the buyer assumes, and a fraction of $1,000 counts as a full $1,000.

Deeds between spouses, between ex-spouses dividing marital property, or between parent and child with no actual payment are exempt under section 76-902(5)(a). Families passing a house down should confirm the exemption wording with the Register of Deeds before recording.

  • Ask the title company for a written tax proration before you sign.
  • Check that every delinquent installment is in the payoff figures.
  • Record the deed in Wahoo, then confirm the Assessor has the new owner's mailing address.

The Register of Deeds also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails an owner when a document is recorded under their name. It is worth setting up for any house that will sit vacant before a sale.

Check water, zoning and land classification first, because a farmstead is valued and regulated differently from a town lot. The county counts 1,500 rural drinking water wells, and state law does not require registration of small wells drilled before September 9, 1993, so a missing record is not unusual for an older place.

  • Wells that can pump more than 50 gallons a minute must be registered and permitted through the local natural resource district.
  • Saunders County is a zoned county, so ask before assuming a land split or second dwelling is allowed.
  • Dryland crop ground covers 51 percent of the county's land and irrigated ground 23 percent, and the mix on a parcel affects its farm valuation.

Nebraska's seller disclosure law, section 76-2,120, asks sellers of one-to-four-unit residential property to state the condition of the electrical, heating, water and sewer systems in writing. A fiduciary selling for an estate is generally excused unless that person lived in the home.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Saunders County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Treasurer at 433 N Chestnut, Suite 201, in Wahoo, mail to PO Box 337, or use Nebraska Taxes Online. The office phone is 402-443-8128.

faqs.q: How do I find a recorded deed in Saunders County?
faqs.a: Deeds from 1997 to the present are searchable on Nebraska Deeds Online. For older records, call the Register of Deeds at 402-443-8111, Suite 203 of the Wahoo courthouse.

faqs.q: Do I owe stamp tax if I deed my house to my child?
faqs.a: Not if no actual payment changes hands. Nebraska exempts deeds between parent and child without actual consideration under section 76-902(5)(a). A sale at a stated price is taxed at $3.32 per $1,000 before 2032.

faqs.q: Is farmland assessed the same as a house in Saunders County?
faqs.a: No. The Assessor values homes and commercial property at 100 percent of market value and agricultural and horticultural land at 75 percent, as of January 1.

faqs.q: Who pays the current year's tax when a Saunders County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The purchase contract and the title company decide how the year is split. Ask for the proration in writing, and make sure any delinquent installment is paid from your proceeds at closing.
